_meta.source: NEC Table 250.122 - Minimum Size Equipment Grounding Conductors for Grounding Raceway and Equipment. Sized by the RATING OF THE OVERCURRENT DEVICE ahead of the circuit, not by the ungrounded conductor size.
_meta.caveat: Entered from the author's memory and NOT independently verified. Lower confidence than the deep-research-verified Table 9 data. See VERIFICATION.md section 11 before relying on this.
_meta.notes: Rows are looked up as 'first row whose ocpd rating is >= the device rating', which is how the table is applied. Intermediate device ratings the printed table may or may not list separately (e.g. 30 A and 40 A, which historically also mapped to 10 AWG Cu / 8 AWG Al) resolve to the same answer under that lookup, so their presence or absence does not change results. The 4000 A aluminum cell is null because the author could not choose between 750 and 800 kcmil with confidence - the app reports 'unverified' rather than guessing.

companionRules.250.122(A): The EGC need not be larger than the circuit conductors supplying the equipment.
companionRules.250.122(B): Where ungrounded conductors are increased in size from the minimum size that has sufficient ampacity for the intended installation, the EGC shall be increased in size proportionately to the circular-mil area of the ungrounded conductors.
companionRules.250.122(D): For motor circuits the EGC is sized on the branch-circuit short-circuit and ground-fault protective device rating, subject to 250.122(A).
companionRules.250.122(F): Where conductors are run in parallel in multiple raceways, a full-size EGC sized per this table is required in EACH raceway - the EGC is not divided among the raceways.
companionRules.250.120(B): Aluminum EGCs are not permitted in direct contact with masonry or earth, in corrosive conditions, or within 18 in. of earth.
